sources.title: Bleeding

facts.text: For a nosebleed, lean forward rather than back so that blood is not swallowed, and pinch the soft part of the nose closed for 10 minutes.
If a nosebleed continues after 20 minutes, the person should get medical care.
A burn should be cooled under cool running water; Taiwan health agencies advise 15 to 30 minutes, and ice water should not be used.
Health agencies advise against putting butter, oil, or home remedies on burns, and against breaking blisters.
During a seizure, nothing should be put in the person's mouth because it can hurt the teeth or jaw; the tongue cannot be swallowed.
During a seizure, move hard objects away, turn the person gently onto one side, and call for emergency help if the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes.
After a snakebite, do not cut the wound or try to suck out the venom; stay calm, remove rings and watches before swelling starts, and get medical care quickly.
After a snakebite, do not try to catch or handle the snake.
If someone swallows poison, do not make the person vomit unless poison control or a health professional says to, and do not give anything by mouth to an unconscious person.
If blood soaks through a cloth on a wound, do not remove it; put another cloth on top and keep pressing, because lifting it to check can make bleeding harder to stop.

notes: 本文只寫健康機構一致的基本建議，不寫藥物或醫療處置。
